title: Integrated DI Sets (3+ Charts)
tagline: Year 4 — Three or more tables or charts about the same entities: combining sales, costs and staffing to answer each question

introduction.overview: An integrated set gives three or more data sources (here sales, cost percentages and staffing) about the same regions or products. Each question needs a few cells from different sources combined by a product, a ratio or a sum. The method is to build one working table of derived values (cost, profit, growth, revenue per employee) for each entity and answer every question from it.
introduction.placementRelevance: Integrated sets are the longest DI items in company tests; building the working table once saves time on all questions.
introduction.realWorldContext: Management reports combine finance, headcount and sales tables in exactly this way.

learningObjectives: Build a working table of derived values

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Cost = sales × cost %. Profit = sales − cost. Productivity = sales ÷ employees. Growth = change ÷ old.

coreDefinitions: Working table: your own table of derived values.
Growth: percentage change over a period.
Margin: profit as a percentage of sales.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Several sources are one table split into pieces. Rejoin them and the questions become lookups.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For each entity compute cost, profit and revenue per employee once; then answer from your table.

mainNarrative: North: sales rose from 200 to 230 (15% growth), cost 60% of 230 = 138, profit 92; revenue per employee 230 × 100 ÷ 400 = ₹57.5 lakh.
South: sales 330, cost 55% = 181.5, profit 148.5, growth 10%, revenue per employee ₹60 lakh.
East: sales 180, cost 65% = 117, profit 63, growth 20%, revenue per employee ₹60 lakh.
West: sales 260, cost 50% = 130, profit 130, growth 4%, revenue per employee ₹52 lakh.
Total 2023 sales are ₹1,000 crore; total profit is 92 + 148.5 + 63 + 130 = 433.5, a margin of 43.35%.

deepDiveAspects.title: Different bases
deepDiveAspects.content: Cost % applies to 2023 sales only; do not apply it to 2022.

deepDiveAspects.title: Productivity versus profit
deepDiveAspects.content: A region can have high revenue per employee and low profit.

solvedExamples.title: Cost and profit
solvedExamples.question: North: 2023 sales ₹230 crore, cost 60% of sales. What is the profit?

solvedExamples.title: Productivity
solvedExamples.question: North: sales ₹230 crore with 400 employees. Revenue per employee in ₹ lakh?

solvedExamples.title: Growth
solvedExamples.question: West sales rose from ₹250 crore to ₹260 crore. Growth?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Compute cost, profit, growth and revenue per employee for each entity once.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying a % to the wrong year
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Read which year the % refers to.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Profit must be less than sales.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write derived columns beside the tables.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: An integrated set is one table in disguise.
